## How it works

- [statement] The February 28, 2026 PowerShell walkthrough obtains Atlas service identifiers, creates the Azure endpoint with manual approval, reads the NIC private IP, and registers the interface with Atlas. It corroborates the staged process but does not supply a tested Bicep module. (medium confidence) — https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1 · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] If Azure endpoint creation fails with LinkedAuthorizationFailed because the current tenant is not authorized to access the linked subscription, Atlas documents adding --manual-request true to the Azure CLI command and running it again. In Bicep, the manualPrivateLinkServiceConnections property is the one Microsoft defines for admins who cannot approve the remote connection; this mapping is an inference, not stated by Atlas. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints
- [statement] If endpoint creation fails with LinkedAuthorizationFailed because the current tenant is not authorized to access the linked subscription, Atlas documents adding --manual-request true to the Azure CLI command and running it again. The corresponding Azure resource property is manualPrivateLinkServiceConnections, which Microsoft defines for network admins who cannot approve connections to the remote resource. Atlas does not itself map the flag to Bicep; that mapping is an inference. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The Bicep resource is Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints. Its properties include subnet (with id) and manualPrivateLinkServiceConnections, whose connection properties include privateLinkServiceId (the resource ID of the private link service). For Atlas on Azure, the target is the Atlas-provisioned private link service, whose resource ID is /subscriptions/{SUBSCRIPTION-ID}/resourceGroups/{RESOURCE-GROUP-ID}/providers/Microsoft.Network/privateLinkServices/{ENDPOINT-SERVICE-NAME}, built from the endpoint service name that Atlas returns (for example pls_<atlas private endpoint ID>), not the Atlas project ID. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md, https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1
- [statement] Gate automation on readiness: Atlas can return INITIATING while its service provisions, and the connection becomes usable after Atlas finishes configuration and reports AVAILABLE. Use status polling instead of assuming an ARM deployment success completes the Atlas connection. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Treat deployment as a staged workflow: create the Atlas Private Link Service, create the Azure consumer endpoint, then register that endpoint with Atlas. Mapping the Azure stage to Bicep is an implementation inference from the documented resource schema and Atlas workflow. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints, https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1
- [statement] For Atlas-owned service approval, use the manual connection path. Microsoft defines manualPrivateLinkServiceConnections for administrators without approval access to the remote resource; the Atlas CLI example and firsthand walkthrough both use --manual-request true. Translating that flag to the Bicep property is an explicit implementation inference. (high confidence) Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md ; https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1 — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md, https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1
- [statement] After Azure creates the endpoint, obtain its resource ID and NIC private IP, then call atlas privateEndpoints azure interfaces create with the Atlas endpointServiceId, --privateEndpointId and --privateEndpointIpAddress. Azure resource creation alone does not finish Atlas registration. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints
- [statement] After registration, retrieve the Atlas private endpoint-specific connection string for the application. The firsthand walkthrough retrieves connectionStrings.privateEndpoint, and the independent Terraform proof of concept demonstrates a -pl-0 endpoint-aware URI. (medium confidence) Sources: https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1 ; https://github.com/eugenebogaart/Atlas-Azure-Link — https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1 · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://github.com/eugenebogaart/Atlas-Azure-Link
- [statement] Atlas documentation limits this private endpoint feature to M10 or higher; Microsoft’s Atlas landing-zone repository likewise identifies a minimum M10 dedicated cluster. A deployment targeting Free or Flex should not assume this feature is available. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-configure-private-endpoints.md ; https://github.com/Azure/mongodb-atlas-landing-zone-accelerator — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-configure-private-endpoints.md · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://github.com/Azure/mongodb-atlas-landing-zone-accelerator
- [statement] Brief Connect demonstrates Bicep parameter files alongside separate Atlas provisioning scripts, but its standard infrastructure guide explicitly excludes hardened VNet/private-endpoint environments and directs those deployments to tailored support. It is evidence for mixed orchestration, not a complete Atlas private endpoint Bicep recipe. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-29) — https://docs.brief-connect.com/Product-Release-Notes/Brief-Connect-v2.5.x-New-Dashboard-Infrastructure-Release-Notes/ · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://docs.brief-connect.com/Product-Release-Notes/Brief-Connect-v2.6.x-Infrastructure/
- [statement] Keep the Atlas endpoint-service ID separate from the Azure Private Link service resource ID: the former identifies the Atlas interface-registration operation; the latter targets the Azure endpoint connection. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://jaliyaudagedara.blogspot.com/2026/02/connecting-azure-to-mongodb-atlas-via.html?m=1
- [statement] Gate application rollout on Atlas reporting the endpoint service and endpoint as Available. Azure resource provisioning success alone is insufficient evidence that Atlas connectivity is ready. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-cluster-private-endpoint.md · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.network/privateendpoints
- [statement] The independent Atlas-Azure-Link repository demonstrates automation spanning both Atlas and Azure providers, including a private endpoint and a client connection. It is Terraform evidence for orchestration, not a Bicep implementation or a current provider-version recommendation. (low confidence) — https://github.com/eugenebogaart/Atlas-Azure-Link · keywords: Atlas Bicep Private Endpoint
